(Schoch et al. 2001, PMID 11691998); "VAMP1 is crucial for vesicle fusion at presynaptic neuromuscular junction (NMJ)." (Salpietro et al. 2017, PMID 28253535)
species_evidence: mouse hippocampal neurons (synaptobrevin 2 knockout with synaptobrevin 1 rescue and knockdown); mouse forebrain neurons (synaptobrevin 2 knockout); human patients with homozygous VAMP1 variants and VAMP1 mutant mice
reading: VAMP1 (synaptobrevin 1) is an alternative to VAMP2 as the vesicle SNARE: it supports release where it is expressed and in proportion to its amount, with less efficiency than VAMP2, and endogenous VAMP1 leaves forebrain neurons that lack VAMP2 with almost no fast release. So it joins every vesicle entity VAMP2 belongs to with a share of VAMP2's membership weight equal to its share of the two genes' brain expression, and the pair counts as one member, the larger of the two, in the complex gate. The share is an mRNA ratio and does not carry VAMP1's lower efficiency, so it is an upper bound on VAMP1's functional share in the forebrain
